newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland's Gdansk to issue muni bond in Oct/Nov.
newsitem.headline: Poland's Gdansk to issue muni bond in Oct/Nov.

text.p: The Polish city of Gdansk will offer a 10.7 million zloty tranche of municipal bonds to investors in late October or early November, its deputy mayor said on Monday.

Longin Mazewski told Reuters the three banks in the lead group -- Bank Gdanski, Bank Handlowy w Warszawie SA and Merrill Lynch -- would each place one-third of the tranche, which is part of a 99.3 million zloty, three-year programme.
"In late October or early November Gdansk wants to issue the first tranche of its municipal bonds. The value of the tranche is set at 10.7 million zlotys," Mazewski said.
He said Bank Gdanski would place the bonds with investors in northern Poland, Bank Handlowy would place them throughout the country and Merrill Lynch would place them abroad.
The dates and size of further tranches would be determined later depending on the city's needs, Mazewski said.

The floating rate bonds, due in 2004, are to be denominated in zlotys and offered in six tranches over three years, with interest linked to the yields of 52-week treasury bonds, Gdansk's mayor announced in March.
The proceeds will be used mainly for rebuilding a road and buying new buses and trams.
